title: Thermal Pleasure and Alliesthesia in the Built Environment
research_question: The aim of this thesis is to propose the physiological concept of alliesthesia as a suitable framework for understanding thermal environmental perception under dynamic or non-isothermal conditions.

participants.description: University-aged subjects (multiple cohorts across three laboratory experiments: 13 subjects for whole-body alliesthesia, 53 subjects for contact heating, and 35 subjects for air movement). Gender distribution varied across experiments.

stimuli_or_exposures.description: Dynamic and non-isothermal indoor thermal environments, including sequential temperature step-changes, ramps, drifts, asymmetric exposures, moderate local skin temperature changes (contact heating of hands/feet, targeted air movement to the back of the neck), and varying air movement patterns (sinusoidal, square, constant, saw-tooth profiles).

findings.mechanism: Contemporary physiological theory has superseded control theory, indicating thermoeffector responses during innocuous thermal exposures are scaled on peripheral rather than core afferent signals.
findings.quote: strong subjective discomfort is not a necessary precondition for thermal pleasure.

findings.mechanism: Alliesthesia is viable even within the thermoneutral zone, though less pronounced and more ambiguous in moderate scenarios.
findings.quote: Alliesthesia remained viable even within the physiological thermoneutral zone, although it was less pronounced and more ambiguous in those moderate scenarios.

findings.antecedent: moderate local skin temperature changes (contrapuntal to whole-body, mean skin temperature) during innocuous exposures at the margins of the thermal comfort zone
findings.quote: Positive hedonic tones were elicited during innocuous exposures at the margins of the thermal comfort zone by applying moderate local skin temperature changes that were contrapuntal to the whole-body, mean skin temperature.

findings.antecedent: dynamic discharge rate of cutaneous thermoreceptors
findings.mechanism: Observations of local skin temperature during asymmetric exposures indicate this underlying mechanism.
findings.quote: Observations of local skin temperature during asymmetric exposures indicate that the underlying mechanism driving a spatial alliesthesial response is the dynamic discharge rate of cutaneous thermoreceptors.

findings.antecedent: locally applied stimuli that contrast the whole-body thermal state (in both warm and cool conditions)
findings.mechanism: Interpreted through the spatial alliesthesia framework.
findings.quote: In both warm and cool conditions, whole-body thermal pleasure was elicited from locally applied stimuli that contrast the whole-body thermal state.
the hedonic tone attached to thermal environmental stimuli, both localised and whole-body, exhibited pronounced between-subject variability.

findings.antecedent: intensity of subjects’ displeasure in the preconditioning environment
findings.consequent: tone and magnitude of thermal pleasure response to localised thermal stimuli
findings.mechanism: This was identified as the most useful variable for distinguishing the response.
moderators_reported: intensity of subjects’ displeasure in the preconditioning environment
findings.quote: The most useful variable for distinguishing the tone and magnitude of thermal pleasure response to localised thermal stimuli was the intensity of the subjects’ displeasure in the preconditioning environment.

findings.antecedent: magnitude of change in local skin temperature
findings.consequent: perceived pleasantness of localised thermal stimuli
findings.quote: The magnitude of change in local skin temperature also had a significant effect on perceived pleasantness of localised thermal stimuli.

findings.antecedent: initial skin temperature and initial thermal pleasure status
findings.mechanism: These were very good predictors in a binomial logistic regression model, improving correct prediction close to 90%.
findings.quote: Initial skin temperature and initial thermal pleasure status were shown to very good predictors of the hedonic response to localised warming, in some instances improving correct prediction close to 90%.

findings.antecedent: body temperatures within the thresholds of the thermoneutral range
findings.mechanism: This is an emerging consensus in contemporary thermophysiological thinking.
findings.quote: Relevant to the discussion of alliesthesia is the emerging consensus that peripheral inputs dominate while body temperatures fall within the thresholds of the thermoneutral range in Figure 2.

findings.mechanism: Heavier reliance on skin rather than core temperature affords the alliesthesial concept much greater relevance to thermal perception in quotidian, built environmental contexts.
findings.quote: Moderate thermal sensations resulting from minor fluctuations in skin temperature could potentially generate a sufficient load-error for alliesthesia.

findings.consequent: perceived as draught (negative valence) or pleasant breeze (positive valence)
findings.mechanism: Grounded in the underlying physiological state and appropriately accommodated within the alliesthesial framework.
findings.quote: The perceptual processes leading to the classification of air movement as either unpleasant draught (negative valence) or pleasant breeze (positive valence) are grounded in the underlying physiological state and as such, appropriately accommodated within the alliesthesial framework.

findings.antecedent: oscillating skin temperatures (from sinusoidal air movement)
findings.consequent: greater number of neuron discharges from cold cutaneous thermoreceptors
findings.mechanism: Due to the relative proximity of cold receptors to skin surface compared to warm counterparts.
findings.quote: oscillating skin temperatures resulting from convective heat loss under sinusoidal air movement would elicit a greater number of neuron discharges from cold cutaneous thermoreceptors during the air speed accelerations than from the warm receptors during the air speed decelerations, simply because of the relative proximity of cold receptors to skin surface compared to the warm counterparts (Hensel, 1981).

findings.antecedent: large volume of thermoafferent traffic (from oscillating skin temperatures)
findings.mechanism: Compared to decayed response from constant air speed, despite the same mean airspeed and ambient temperature.
findings.quote: The large volume of thermoafferent traffic would generated a more perceptible cool sensation compared to the decayed response when exposed to a constant air speed, despite the mean airspeed and ambient temperature being the same under both conditions.

findings.antecedent: localized cooling caused by airflow (contrast to warm global condition)
findings.mechanism: This effect was observed in the Tanabe and Kimura (1994) experiment.
findings.quote: The subjects in the Tanabe and Kimura (1994) experiment would have found the localized cooling caused by airflow a pleasant contrast to the warm global condition – in effect they were enjoying spatial alliesthesia.

mechanisms: The physiological concept of alliesthesia, which links psychological processes with physiological states, provides a unifying framework for understanding thermal perception in dynamic and non-isothermal conditions.
Thermoeffector responses during innocuous thermal exposures are scaled on the basis of peripheral (cutaneous) rather than core afferent signals.

Both the rate-of-change of local skin temperature and regional differences in thermosensitivity across the body surface provide the neurophysiological basis for thermoregulation and thermal perception.
The dynamic discharge rate of cutaneous thermoreceptors is the underlying mechanism driving spatial alliesthesial responses.
moderators: intensity of the subjects’ displeasure in the preconditioning environment
implementation_implications: Targeted thermal stimulation delivered locally by personal environmental control (PEC) systems can increase occupant satisfaction while reducing energy consumption.
PEC systems offer a solution to elicit spatial alliesthesia in free-living environments.
Returning control to individual occupants through adaptive opportunities embedded in fit-out is crucial for successful alliesthesial design strategies.

theory_commitments.specific_claim: The hedonic perception of a thermal stimulus depends on the internal thermal state of the organism, such that a stimulus perceived as neutral or unpleasant in a comfortable state can be perceived as pleasurable when the organism is in a state of thermal discomfort.

mechanism_chain.description: A change in thermal conditions following a state of strong subjective discomfort leads to a physiological and perceptual shift towards comfort, which is experienced as thermal pleasure, consistent with the principle of alliesthesia.
